note: Per-chapter drafting knowledge, keyed by the chapter IDs in data/drhp_structure.json. NARRATIVE chapters carry an 'instruction' and 'context_fields' used to build a constrained LLM prompt, plus a deterministic 'fallback' so the product works identically with no API key. BOILERPLATE chapters carry 'clauses' — standard offer-document text with issuer fields merged in, always marked for merchant-banker finalisation. FACTUAL chapters are built in code from issuer data because they are tables, not prose; they appear here only where they need supporting narrative. Interpolation uses {dotted.path} against the issuer data, plus a {computed.*} namespace of values derived arithmetically from it. A block may carry "when": "computed.flag" or "!computed.flag" to include it conditionally.

I.2.title: Presentation of Financial, Industry and Market Data

clauses.p: Unless stated otherwise, the financial information in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus is derived from the Restated Financial Statements of the Company for the financial years {computed.financialYearsList}, prepared in accordance with the Companies Act and restated in accordance with the ICDR Regulations.

The Company's financial year commences on 1 April and ends on 31 March of the succeeding year. References to a particular financial year are to the twelve-month period ended on 31 March of that year. All figures are presented in Indian Rupees. Figures expressed in crore represent ten million and figures expressed in lakh represent one hundred thousand.

Certain figures have been subjected to rounding adjustments. Accordingly, figures shown as totals in certain tables may not be the exact arithmetic aggregation of the figures that precede them. All percentage figures have been calculated on the basis of unrounded amounts.
All references to "INR", "Rs." or "Rupees" are to Indian Rupees, the lawful currency of the Republic of India. The Company has presented all financial information in Indian Rupees.

Industry and market data used in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus has been obtained from publicly available sources and from industry publications. Such data involves risks, assumptions and limitations, and has not been independently verified by the Company or by the Lead Manager. The data may be defined differently by different sources, and accordingly investors should not place undue reliance on it.

clauses.note: The merchant banker must attribute each industry statistic to a named, dated public source before this chapter is finalised. Statistics carried without attribution are a routine exchange observation.

clauses.p: This Draft Red Herring Prospectus contains certain forward-looking statements. Statements that are not statements of historical fact, and which include words such as "anticipate", "believe", "expect", "estimate", "intend", "objective", "plan", "propose", "project", "seek", "will", "would" or other words or phrases of similar import, are forward-looking statements.

All forward-looking statements are subject to risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could cause actual results to differ materially from those contemplated. Important factors that could cause such a difference include, but are not limited to, the Company's ability to retain its principal customers, movements in the price and availability of raw materials, the Company's ability to fund and commission the capital expenditure described under "Objects of the Issue", changes in the regulatory environment applicable to the {business.industry} sector, general economic and business conditions in India, and the other matters described under "Risk Factors".

Forward-looking statements reflect the Company's current views as at the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus and are not a guarantee of future performance. Neither the Company, its Directors, the Lead Manager, nor any of their respective affiliates has any obligation to update or otherwise revise any forward-looking statement to reflect events or circumstances arising after the date of this document.

In accordance with the requirements of SEBI and the SME Platform, the Company and the Lead Manager will ensure that investors are informed of material developments from the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus until the date of allotment.

II.1.title: Risk Factors
II.1.instruction: Draft the Risk Factors chapter of an Indian SME IPO offer document. Open with the standard prefatory paragraph explaining that investors should read the section carefully and that the risks are not exhaustive and are not in order of priority. Then draft INTERNAL (company-specific) risk factors derived ONLY from the issuer data supplied, followed by EXTERNAL/INDUSTRY risks and ISSUE-RELATED risks. Each risk factor must be numbered, begin with a short bold-style heading sentence stating the risk, and continue with two to four sentences explaining the exposure and its potential consequence for the business, results of operations, cash flows or financial condition. Use the restrained, formal register of a filed prospectus: no marketing language, no reassurance, no superlatives, and no mitigating claims that the issuer data does not support. Quantify wherever the data allows (customer shares, revenue, borrowings, capacity utilisation). Where litigation or a related-party dependency exists in the issuer data, it MUST appear as a risk factor. Do not invent any fact, number, customer name or event that is not present in the issuer data.
must_cover: litigation and regulatory proceedings, if any exist in the data
related-party dependence, if any exists in the data
issue-related risks including SME platform liquidity

fallback.p: An investment in equity shares involves a high degree of risk. Investors should carefully consider all the information in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, including the risks and uncertainties described below, together with the Restated Financial Statements, before making an investment decision. If any of the following risks, or other risks that are not currently known or are currently deemed immaterial, actually occur, the business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition of the Company could be materially and adversely affected, the trading price of the equity shares could decline, and investors may lose all or part of their investment. The risks below are not exhaustive and are not set out in any order of priority or of the magnitude of their potential impact.

1. The Company derives a substantial proportion of its revenue from a limited number of customers. The Company has disclosed its principal customers and their respective contribution to revenue as follows: {business.top_customers}. The loss of any of these customers, a reduction in the volume of orders placed by them, a renegotiation of commercial terms, or a delay or default in payment by them, could materially and adversely affect the Company's revenue, profitability and cash flows. The Company does not have committed offtake arrangements that guarantee minimum volumes over the life of its supply relationships.

2. The Company is dependent on a limited supplier base and on the price of its principal raw materials. {business.suppliers} An interruption in supply, a deterioration in the commercial terms available to the Company, or a sustained increase in input prices that the Company is unable to pass on to customers under its existing pricing arrangements, would compress margins and adversely affect results of operations.

2. The Company is dependent on its ability to recruit, deploy and retain personnel at the cost assumed in its customer contracts. The Company has described its workforce as follows: {business.employees}. Increases in statutory minimum wages, provident fund or other employment costs that cannot be passed through to customers under existing contracts would directly compress margins, and an inability to deploy personnel to the standard required could result in the loss of a contract.

3. The Company's operations are working-capital intensive and its operating cash flow has been lower than its reported profit. Revenue from operations for the latest financial year was INR {financials.revenue_latest_year} crore and profit after tax was INR {financials.pat_latest_year} crore, while net cash generated from operating activities was INR {computed.cashFlowLatest} crore. Any extension of customer credit periods, build-up of inventory, or delay in collections could constrain liquidity and increase the Company's reliance on borrowed funds.

4. The Company's manufacturing operations are concentrated at a limited number of facilities and depend on continued capacity utilisation. {business.plants_capacity} Any disruption at these facilities arising from equipment failure, industrial action, fire, natural calamity, interruption of power or water supply, or the suspension or non-renewal of a statutory consent, would directly interrupt the Company's ability to supply its customers.

5. A portion of the Net Proceeds is to be applied to capital expenditure that has not yet been incurred, and the Company has not entered into definitive arrangements for its entire proposed deployment. The proposed deployment described under "Objects of the Issue" is based on management estimates and has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution. Cost overruns, delays in commissioning, or a failure to secure the volumes assumed for the additional capacity could mean that the expected benefits of the expansion are not realised.

6. The Company is party to outstanding proceedings, an adverse outcome in which could affect its financial condition. {legal.litigation} Legal and regulatory proceedings are inherently uncertain, and the Company may be required to make provisions or payments, or may incur costs in defending such matters, that adversely affect its results of operations.

7. The Company transacts with entities connected to its promoters, and those relationships may not be on arm's-length terms. {management.related_parties} Any adverse change in these arrangements, a determination that they were not conducted at arm's length, or a conflict between the interests of the promoters and those of the Company, could adversely affect the Company's operations and reputation.

8. The Company has outstanding indebtedness of INR {indebtedness.total_borrowings} crore, and its financing arrangements contain restrictive covenants. {indebtedness.lenders} These arrangements require the Company to service interest and principal irrespective of its operating performance, restrict its ability to incur further indebtedness or create security, and may require lender consent for certain corporate actions. A breach of covenant could result in acceleration of repayment or enforcement of security over the Company's assets.

9. The Company depends on its promoters and a small senior management team. {promoters.promoter_names} have led the Company's operations and hold key customer and supplier relationships. The loss of the services of the promoters or of other key managerial personnel, or an inability to attract and retain qualified personnel, could adversely affect the Company's ability to operate and to execute its stated strategy.

10. The Company operates in the {business.industry} sector and its performance is linked to conditions in that sector and in the broader economy. A slowdown in end-user demand, changes in customer production plans, technological change affecting the Company's products, or the entry of competitors with greater financial or technical resources, could reduce the Company's volumes and pricing. The Company competes with both organised and unorganised participants, some of whom may accept lower margins.

11. The Company's operations are subject to extensive regulation and require statutory approvals which must be maintained and periodically renewed. {legal.approvals} The failure to obtain, maintain or renew any material approval, or a change in the applicable regulatory regime including in environmental, labour or taxation law, could interrupt operations or increase the Company's cost of compliance.

12. There has been no public market for the equity shares and an active or sustained trading market may not develop. The equity shares are proposed to be listed on {issue_structure.listing_platform}. Securities listed on the SME platform are typically less liquid than securities listed on the main board, are traded in specified lot sizes, and may exhibit greater price volatility. Investors may be unable to sell the equity shares at or above the Issue price, or at all.

13. The Issue price is not indicative of the market price of the equity shares after the Issue. The Issue price of {issue.price_band} has been determined by the Company in consultation with the Lead Manager on the basis of the factors described under "Basis for Issue Price", and should not be taken to be indicative of the market price of the equity shares after listing. The market price may be affected by the Company's results, conditions in the {business.industry} sector, and general market conditions, and may decline below the Issue price.

14. The Company's ability to pay dividends in the future will depend on its earnings, capital requirements and financing arrangements. {dividend.dividend_history} The Company intends to retain earnings to fund the expansion described under "Objects of the Issue", and there is no assurance that it will declare dividends in any future period.

clauses.p: In accordance with the ICDR Regulations and the Depositories Act, 1996, the Equity Shares will be Allotted only in dematerialised form. Where Equity Shares are registered in the names of two or more persons, they will be deemed to hold them as joint tenants with the benefit of survivorship, subject to the provisions of the Articles.

In accordance with Section 72 of the Companies Act, the sole or first Applicant, together with any joint Applicants, may nominate a person in whom, in the event of the death of the sole or all joint Applicants, the Equity Shares would vest. The procedure set out below is subject to the ICDR Regulations and the SEBI circulars in force at the time the Issue opens. Applicants are advised to inform themselves of the procedure applicable at that time, and no reliance should be placed on this summary alone.

list: Indian nationals resident in India who are competent to contract under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, applying in single or joint names;
Hindu Undivided Families, through the karta, with the Application made in the name of the karta;
companies, corporate bodies and societies registered under applicable law in India and authorised to invest in equity shares;
mutual funds registered with SEBI, and venture capital funds and alternative investment funds registered with SEBI, subject to their respective investment restrictions;

list: An Applicant submits the Application Form to a Designated Intermediary, or applies online through the internet banking facility of an SCSB.
The Application Form authorises the SCSB to block the Application Amount in the ASBA Account named in the form.

The Application Amount remains blocked in the ASBA Account until the Designated Date, or until the Application is withdrawn, rejected or unsuccessful, and continues to earn interest for the Applicant during that period in accordance with the terms of the account.
The Applicant may not withdraw the authorisation to block, other than in the circumstances permitted under the ICDR Regulations.
On the Designated Date, the SCSB transfers the amount corresponding to the Equity Shares Allotted to the Public Issue Account and unblocks the balance.

clauses.p: A Retail Individual Investor whose Application Amount does not exceed the threshold prescribed by SEBI for the UPI Mechanism may apply through that mechanism. The procedure is as follows:

list: The Applicant creates a UPI ID with a bank or a payment service provider whose application is listed on the website of the National Payments Corporation of India as eligible for public issue applications.
The Applicant enters the UPI ID in the Application Form and submits it to a Designated Intermediary.
The Designated Intermediary uploads the Application on the electronic bidding platform of the SME Platform, and the Sponsor Bank initiates a UPI Mandate Request to the Applicant.
The Applicant approves the UPI Mandate Request on the UPI application, which blocks the Application Amount in the ASBA Account.
The Applicant must approve the mandate within the time prescribed. An unapproved mandate results in the Application not being considered.

clauses.p: An Applicant using the UPI Mechanism should ensure that the bank account linked to the UPI ID has sufficient balance, that the UPI ID furnished is correct, and that the mandate is approved from the mobile number registered with the bank.

list: Application Forms are available with the Designated Intermediaries and on the websites of the SME Platform and the Lead Manager.
Applications must be for the minimum Application size specified in the Red Herring Prospectus, and in multiples of the Bid Lot thereafter.
Applications must be made only in dematerialised form. The DP ID, Client ID and PAN furnished must match the depository records exactly.

The Permanent Account Number of each Applicant is mandatory, irrespective of the Application Amount, other than for Applications on behalf of the central or state government, for officials appointed by a court, and for residents of the state of Sikkim, subject to verification.
An Applicant should submit only one Application Form. Multiple Applications made by the same person, other than as expressly permitted, are liable to be rejected.
On submission, the Designated Intermediary issues an acknowledgement to the Applicant. The acknowledgement is not an acceptance of the Application.

clauses.p: Applications are liable to be rejected on any of the following grounds, among others:

list: the Application Amount is not blocked, or the ASBA Account has insufficient funds;
the Application is for a number of Equity Shares below the minimum Application size, or not in multiples of the Bid Lot;
the DP ID, Client ID or PAN is incorrect, illegible or does not match the depository records;
the PAN is not furnished, except where expressly exempt;
the Application Form is not signed by the sole or first Applicant, or by all joint Applicants;
the Application is submitted without the authorisation to block funds, or the UPI Mandate Request is not approved within the prescribed time;
the depository account is suspended, frozen or closed, or the details furnished relate to an account that does not exist;
the Application is by a person not competent to contract, including a minor other than through a guardian;
multiple Applications are made by the same Applicant otherwise than as permitted;
the Application is by a person prohibited from investing in the Equity Shares under applicable law, or is in contravention of any applicable investment limit;
the Application is submitted to a person other than a Designated Intermediary, or at a location other than a designated collection point;
the Application Form is incomplete, contains inconsistent or contradictory particulars, or is not made in the prescribed form; or
the Application is withdrawn or revised otherwise than in the manner permitted.

The Registrar to the Issue, in consultation with the Company, the Lead Manager and the SME Platform, may reject an Application on any other ground consistent with the ICDR Regulations and the applicable SEBI circulars.

VII.4.title: Restrictions on Foreign Ownership of Indian Securities

clauses.p: Foreign investment in Indian securities is regulated by the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 and the rules and regulations made under it, read with the consolidated Foreign Direct Investment Policy issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Government of India, as amended from time to time. Under the current framework, foreign direct investment in most sectors is permitted under the automatic route, subject to the sectoral caps, entry conditions and pricing guidelines prescribed.

Foreign Portfolio Investors registered with SEBI may invest in the Equity Shares subject to the limits prescribed under the applicable regulations, including the limit on the holding of a single Foreign Portfolio Investor together with its investor group, and the aggregate limit applicable to all Foreign Portfolio Investors in an Indian company. Where an investment exceeds the prescribed threshold, it is reclassified as foreign direct investment in the manner prescribed.

Eligible NRIs may invest in the Equity Shares on a repatriation or a non-repatriation basis, subject to the conditions and limits prescribed under FEMA and the rules made under it. An Eligible NRI applying on a repatriation basis must do so through the appropriate account and must furnish the particulars required in the Application Form.

clauses.h: Restrictions on investment from certain jurisdictions

clauses.p: An entity of a country which shares a land border with India, or where the beneficial owner of an investment into India is situated in or is a citizen of such a country, may invest only under the government route, in accordance with the consolidated Foreign Direct Investment Policy. Any transfer of ownership resulting in such beneficial ownership requires government approval.

The issue and transfer of the Equity Shares to a person resident outside India is subject to the pricing guidelines and the reporting requirements prescribed under FEMA. The Company will comply with the applicable reporting requirements in respect of any Allotment made to a person resident outside India.

The Equity Shares have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933 or under the securities laws of any state of the United States, and may not be offered or sold within the United States except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of that Act and applicable state securities laws.

clauses.note: Foreign investment conditions, sectoral caps and the applicable thresholds change frequently. The Lead Manager and legal counsel must confirm the position applicable to the Company's sector as at the date of the Red Herring Prospectus.
